content: Vaccines reduce the risk of getting infectious diseases by working with the body's natural defenses to build protection. Recommended vaccines and schedules vary by age, health, and local public-health guidance. Ask a qualified healthcare professional or local health authority about personal vaccination decisions; this prototype does not provide a verified clinic schedule.

content: Protecting and improving children's health is important. The World Health Organization notes that child health depends on access to healthcare as well as nutrition, safety, and supportive conditions for growth and development. This general information does not describe services or hours at a specific hospital and is not personal medical advice.

Cardiovascular diseases are disorders of the heart and blood vessels. The World Health Organization identifies tobacco use, unhealthy diet, physical inactivity, and harmful alcohol use among important behavioral risk factors. Chest pain or difficulty breathing can require urgent assessment; this chatbot cannot diagnose symptoms, so seek emergency care for a possible emergency.
source: World Health Organization, Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), fact sheet, 2025-07-31, https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/cardiovascular-diseases-(cvds)
